subject.title: 2026.7.1 gateway crash-loop: legacy memory sidecar `meta`/`chunks` conflicts are fatal while `files` conflicts auto-resolve

question: Which persisted-state authority rule should Memory Core use when legacy `meta` or `chunks` rows conflict with canonical per-agent SQLite rows during upgrade?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the crash-loop but cannot safely decide whether divergent metadata is disposable or whether same-key chunk divergence can contain unique user-derived state; a blanket recovery rule could trade availability for silent state loss.

options.title: Use table-specific authority
options.body: Keep canonical derived-cache rows, define canonical metadata ownership, and preserve or explicitly reconcile divergent chunks before archiving the sidecar.

options.title: Always keep canonical SQLite
options.body: Treat every conflicting legacy table as superseded, archive the sidecar, and accept that divergent legacy chunk values may be discarded.

options.title: Keep fail-closed conflicts
options.body: Preserve strict conflict blocking but make `doctor --fix` provide a safe inspected backup-and-resolution workflow that actually converges.

recommendation.title: Use table-specific authority
recommendation.body: Keep canonical derived-cache rows, define canonical metadata ownership, and preserve or explicitly reconcile divergent chunks before archiving the sidecar.

likelyOwner.reason: The original migration history connects this owner directly to the cross-table persisted-state contract that needs definition.
